own_solution.law: Projectile motion gives flight time t = 2v sin(theta)/g and horizontal range R = v² sin(2theta)/g. At theta = 35°, R = (400/9.8) sin(70°). Lowering the current launch direction by 14° gives theta = 21° and R = (400/9.8) sin(42°).
assumptions: Uniform downward gravitational acceleration of 9.8 m/s².
Air resistance is neglected as stated.
Launch and landing elevations are equal.
The ramp beside the launch point does not intersect the ball's trajectory.
The launcher returns to its stated initial setting after each earlier trial.

defect_reasons.rendering_not_minimal: T9D35 and TC550 specify an unquantified 'few degrees', whereas their corresponding numerical variants TFC29 and T9417 specify 14°, violating the requirement that variants preserve the same number and unit.

notes: The base projectile problem and all individual added-sentence problems have determinate answers. The invalid verdict concerns the required numerical matching of variants. The explicit initial-setting clarification makes the current-trial lowering consistent with the base description; the reset after every trial disconnects earlier adjustments from the current range.
